newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Buthelezi to act as president while Mandela away.
newsitem.headline: Buthelezi to act as president while Mandela away.

text.p: Zulu leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi will run South Africa while President Nelson Mandela and his deputy attend the World Economic Forum in Switzerland, Mandela told the Senate in Cape Town on Friday.

In what political analysts said was a gesture of reconciliation towards the man seen as his main black rival, Mandela plainly surprised the assembly by announcing: "I have decided to appoint the Minister of Home Affairs Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi as acting president of the country."
Both Mandela and deputy president Thabo Mbeki are due to attend the annual Davos forum, where Mandela will deliver a speech on the problem of AIDS.

Mandela will be out of the country for two days. His announcement to the Senate provoked some uncertain laughter, as if members were not sure whether Mandela was joking, a Reuter correspondent on the scene said.
Buthelezi strongly denied in a South African television interview on Thursday that his Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) was under severe internal strains because of his autocratic style of leadership.

Intense rivalry between the IFP and the ruling African National Congress of Mandela and Mbeki has been at the root of persisent political violence in the province of KwaZulu-Natal the homeland of South Africa's nine million Zulus.
